subject: Post-call: data sovereignty, retention, and KMS/HSM choices (Finova)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@finova.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — data handling & key management options

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned on scope and what you asked us to follow up on.

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary concern: PII handling across ingestion, logs, and storage. Finova needs strong guarantees around retention windows and proof-of-deletion.
- Residency: Transactions and associated logs for EU customers must remain in EU region.
- Encryption: Preference for customer-managed keys (CMK) where possible; interested in HSM-backed options and attestation.
- Logging: Need clarity on whether logs ever contain plaintext PII and what redaction/pseudonymization controls exist.

Redwood options (brief)
- Hosted with Redwood-managed keys: fastest onboarding; keys managed in cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) with AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended mid-path): We support customer CMKs in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault; we can configure envelope encryption so you control the root key.
- HSM / BYOK: For higher assurance, we offer CloudHSM integrations (AWS CloudHSM) for hosted customers and on-prem Private deployments that can connect to your HSM via KMIP or vendor-specific connectors.
- Private deployment: Full control (VPC/on-prem) with optional on-prem HSM integration; best for strict residency/air-gap policies.

Attachments included: redwood-encryption-options.pdf (summary), sample-data-retention-policy.docx.

Questions you asked us to answer (next steps)
1) Will logs ever contain plaintext PII? If yes, how is it protected and who can access it?
2) For CMK/BYOK, what's the lifecycle? Can you rotate/revoke keys and provide proof of deletion?
3) What attestation/certifications do you offer for HSM-backed keys (FIPS, etc.)?
4) How do you support different retention windows by region and produce audit evidence?

Proposed immediate steps
- I'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive between your security team and our infra/security lead (Marcus Lin). Please share 2x time slots tomorrow or Monday.
- Marcus, can you draft short, concrete answers to the numbered questions above and attach any cert/attestation docs we can share?
- We will load the security questionnaire you sent into our tracker and return an initial pass by EOD Monday.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Lead — FinTech

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — data handling & key management options

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear recap — that helps. A few clarifying questions from our security and procurement teams so we can scope the risk review:

1) Logs and PII: Do any application or access logs contain raw PII (account numbers, SSNs, email addresses) before redaction? If so, what is the retention and access control for those logs?
2) CMK lifecycle: If we provide a CMK (BYOK), can we rotate keys on our cadence? If we request key destruction, what is the proof process?
3) HSM attestations: Can you provide details on the HSM model/certification used for CloudHSM integrations and whether you support FIPS 140-2/FIPS 140-3 validated modules?
4) Cross-region residency: For EU-subject data, can you guarantee processing and storage in EU-only zones (including backups and logs)?
5) Deletion & eDiscovery: If a retention removal is requested, what is Redwood's process to ensure data is removed and how long does it take?

Also — procurement asked for an example of contractual SLAs and any limits on data export.

Can Marcus or Vanessa pick these up? We'd like a written response and any supporting artifacts (attestations, whitepapers) before the technical call.

Thanks,
Hannah Li
Head of InfoSec Programs
Finova Bank

Karthik / Vanessa / Hannah — quick technical notes to start; I'll prepare a short FAQ and attach implementation notes (see kms-implementation-notes.pdf). We can expand for the compliance pack if needed.

1) Logs and PII
- Application telemetry: We do not intentionally log raw PII in application-level telemetry. In cases where log lines could contain user-provided content, we offer two protections: automatic client-side redaction hooks (recommended) and server-side redaction rules.
- Access logs: Access/audit logs (authentication events, API request metadata) do not include plaintext PII by default. Where payload inspection is enabled for debugging, logs are accessible only to a small SRE group and are time-limited.
- Retention: Log retention is configurable per customer (default 90 days). We can set separate retention windows for EU vs US.

2) CMK lifecycle (BYOK)
- Rotation: If you supply a CMK via AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault, you can rotate per your cadence; our envelope keys reference the CMK. We recommend coordinate rotation windows; rotations do not require re-encrypting stored blobs due to envelope encryption.
- Revocation / destruction: If you request key destruction in the cloud KMS, you control the key lifecycle. For evidence, we provide KMS event logs and a signed statement of key state change. For Private deployments where keys are hosted on-prem or in your HSM, you retain physical control and can produce HSM audit logs.

3) HSM attestations
- For hosted CloudHSM we primarily integrate with AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliant modules available). We can provide the vendor attestation and describe the module version used in your tenant.
- For on-prem HSM integrations (KMIP or vendor-specific connectors), attestation responsibility is shared: we can collect and transmit HSM-generated certificates but the primary attestation originates from your HSM appliance.

4) Cross-region residency
- We support region-scoped deployments: data (including backups) and logs can be constrained to EU zones only for EU-subject accounts. We can provide an explicit residency configuration and an audit report showing region IDs for storage and compute.

5) Deletion & eDiscovery
- Retention request: For data removal we run a three-step process: identify (query by tenant/data-id), purge (delete application-level copies and rotate encryption envelope keys), and verify (provide purge report). Typical SLA: initial purge completed within 48–72 hours for hosted customers; certificate of deletion provided within 7 business days.

Artifacts I'll attach: kms-implementation-notes.pdf (technical details), and a short FAQ PDF summarizing the above. Marcus — can you drop the audit attestation (CloudHSM cert) into the drive link Karthik referenced?

We should propose slot options for a 30–45m call: Fri 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 09:00–10:00 PT.
